editorial.headline: Chilli Farming as a Full-Cycle Agricultural Business
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01138 covers chilli cultivation from land preparation to post-harvest handling, and is nationally open to foreign ownership at every listed business scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01138 is the agricultural home for chilli farming. Its scope is not limited to harvesting mature plants; it covers the full chain of cultivation for Capsicum crops, including large chillies, bird’s eye chillies, curly chillies, and paprika. The activity begins with land preparation, seed sowing, nursery work, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling when those steps are carried out as one connected agricultural process.

The record also makes clear that this code includes chilli planting for seed production, specifically seed in the form of grain. That matters because the activity is not only about producing fresh vegetables for the market. It can also describe a cultivation operation whose output supports the next planting cycle through nursery and seed-related work, as long as the activity remains within the stated chilli-farming scope. In plain English, this is a code for operators who are actually growing chilli crops, managing the crop cycle, and handling the immediate post-harvest stage as part of the same farming business.

On scale, the code is broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can describe anything from a small farming operation to a larger agricultural enterprise, provided the registered activity remains chilli cultivation and its included nursery, seed, harvesting, and post-harvest sequence. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is equally direct: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the slim record, so the national reading is that a foreign-owned company may register this activity up to 100% foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also clean, but for a different reason than many low-risk activities. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, according to the recorded rule. This code, however, is not shown as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore simple: KBLI 01138 is nationally open to PMA at 100%, and the Bali record provided here does not block it under the stated moratorium.
